title: Facets: small multiples
explanation: When one chart gets crowded, split it into a grid of small charts, one per group, all with the same axes. These are called **facets** or **small multiples**, and they make comparisons easy.

tasks.teach: **facet_wrap(~ column)** makes one panel per value of the column. The **~** is a tilde (top-left of most keyboards), read as "by".
tasks.prompt: Plot minutes vs score, with one small chart per subject: + facet_wrap(~ subject).
tasks.answer: ggplot(study_log, aes(x = minutes, y = score)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ subject)

tasks.prompt: Last one: one line chart per service: ggplot(subscribers, aes(x = year, y = subscribers)) + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ service).
hints: Same idea, with geom_line() and service.
tasks.answer: ggplot(subscribers, aes(x = year, y = subscribers)) + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ service)

recap: facet_wrap(~ column) splits a chart into small multiples, one per group, with shared axes for easy comparison.
